item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-25aa8359197fb710","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Artículo 19 reported that the first three years of López Obrador’s government were the most violent period against the press on record, documenting 1,945 attacks, 30 journalist killings, and two disappearances; attacks increased 85% and journalist killings doubled compared with the comparable period under Enrique Peña Nieto.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.6","3B.8","3B.10","4B.3","4B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The article covers 2018–2021 and was updated in March 2023; it provides relevant inherited-period context but not a complete 2023 account.","ruler_attribution":"Artículo 19 attributed the deterioration to the López Obrador government and criticized official responses.","limitations":["The source reports an advocacy organization’s findings and does not independently establish causation for every attack."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0b636088626c1ec9","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The Ayotzinapa GIEI said the Army, Navy, and intelligence institutions continued obstructing the investigation into the 43 students’ disappearance, denying or concealing information despite an order from López Obrador to cooperate; the GIEI reported changing military accounts, military infiltration and real-time intelligence, and unresolved arrest warrants.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.9","4B.4","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly reports the GIEI’s March 2023 assessment of ongoing conduct and institutional resistance.","ruler_attribution":"The report states that López Obrador ordered the Army to collaborate, while agencies under his government allegedly withheld information and obstructed the inquiry.","limitations":["The source does not establish whether López Obrador personally ordered or approved the obstruction."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2aebd4dd146638e8","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Amnesty International stated that the López Obrador government had not delivered 800 Army documents requested for the Ayotzinapa investigation, including records concerning the transfer of 17 students; it reported that the GIEI left the investigation after the refusal and that López Obrador began attacks discrediting organizations advising the families.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.9","4B.3","4B.4","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The document was issued in 2024 but describes developments during 2023 and is relevant to the target year.","ruler_attribution":"Amnesty attributed the document refusal and public attacks to the federal government led by López Obrador.","limitations":["This is an urgent-action appeal summarizing reported facts and advocacy concerns rather than a judicial finding."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6269f35c63e1be58","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The Mexican Public Administration Ministry investigated alleged conflicts of interest involving López Obrador, his son José Ramón, and businessman Daniel Chávez, and closed the case for insufficient evidence; it found Chávez was an unpaid honorary Tren Maya supervisor and stated it lacked jurisdiction over some foreign or non-federal conduct.","question_ids":["7B.3","7B.4","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9"],"polarity":"exculpatory","period_fit":"The investigation and closure occurred in 2022, providing relevant integrity context for 2023 but not a 2023 finding.","ruler_attribution":"The SFP issued the exculpatory administrative conclusion; López Obrador publicly denied a conflict of interest.","limitations":["The SFP stated it lacked jurisdiction over some alleged conduct, so the closure was not a universal finding that all allegations were disproven."]},{"source_id":"SRC-74dad96f02de6ed5","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The UN Working Group on Arbitrary Detention’s 2023 Mexico visit identified positive legal institutions, including the National Detention Registry and the torture-prevention mechanism, but found arbitrary detention widespread, citing preventive detention, arraigo, militarized security, excessive force, weak legal assistance, attacks on judicial independence, poor detention conditions, and particular impacts on Indigenous people and migrants.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","4B.4","6B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns the Working Group’s September 2023 visit and contemporaneous conditions.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern Mexico during López Obrador’s presidency but do not attribute each deficiency personally to him.","limitations":["The summary identifies systemic conditions and reforms without quantifying López Obrador’s individual causal responsibility."]},{"source_id":"SRC-256d2acfdc515056","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"After the Guacamaya leak, Sedena reported 6,124 cyberattack attempts from November 2022 to April 2023 and said it implemented software updates, international cybersecurity practices, strengthened protections, and personnel training; it had filed no complaint with the federal prosecutor, classified information about its internal investigation, and a military judge released an accused informatics commander provisionally.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.7","1B.9","1B.10","4B.4","4B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Reports cybersecurity and accountability measures and omissions spanning late 2022 through April 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The reported measures and secrecy were actions of Sedena under López Obrador’s government; the source does not show his personal direction.","limitations":["The source does not assess whether the safeguards were adequate or whether López Obrador approved the classification decision."]},{"source_id":"SRC-acbee5f9051a7827","start_unit":3,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"A Latinus investigation, summarized by Sopitas, alleged that friends of Andrés López Beltrán received more than 100 million pesos in government-linked contracts, including Texcoco projects, and that three companies sharing an address and partners simulated competition; related companies allegedly obtained additional SEDATU and other public-works contracts.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.6","7B.4","7B.5","7B.9","7B.10","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report was published in May 2023 and concerns contracts signed or operating during the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The allegations concern relatives and associates of López Obrador; the source does not establish that he personally directed the contracts.","limitations":["This is a secondary summary of an investigative report and reports allegations rather than final administrative or judicial findings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-41c5d88094e00d9f","start_unit":5,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Centro Prodh reported that reforms extended the armed forces’ public-security role through 2028 and expanded military influence; by July 2023 the National Guard had opened 11,186 internal-affairs files, but only 449 were referred to disciplinary councils, 320 to internal control, and 261 to prosecutors, with insufficient sanctions and continuing alleged extrajudicial executions and military control of investigations and public messaging.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.9","3B.10","4B.4","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly reports legal and institutional developments and accountability data through November 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the expanded military role to reforms and acts during López Obrador’s administration and notes attacks from the presidential tribune against critics.","limitations":["Centro Prodh is an advocacy organization; the figures show referrals and alleged insufficient sanctions but do not by themselves establish every underlying violation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f94c331b84919459","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"A 2023 human-rights and legal study characterized the López Obrador administration as repeatedly criticized for corruption concerns, opaque public-resource management, excessive public-works spending, and authoritarian implementation, and stated that the transparency institution had been paralyzed since 2022; it cited reporting on reduced staffing and increased denials of information and noncompetitive procurement.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.6","5B.5","5B.7","7B.1","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The study appears in the 2023 journal volume, although the page was published in January 2024 and includes 2023 sources.","ruler_attribution":"The study evaluates the federal administration led by López Obrador.","limitations":["The supplied extract is an abstract and bibliography, not the study’s detailed empirical findings; several claims are presented as allegations or cited secondary reporting."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c7128877af4cd1d8","start_unit":3,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"WOLA reported in September 2023 that Sedena did not register its arrests in the legally required National Detention Registry, that military detention statistics appeared significantly underreported, and that authorities had concealed Ayotzinapa information and used Pegasus against activists; it also cited abuses by federal forces and National Guard, alleged crime-scene alteration, and widespread impunity.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.4","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns conditions and institutional conduct reported in September 2023.","ruler_attribution":"WOLA described these as actions or failures of institutions operating under López Obrador’s government, without proving his personal involvement in each event.","limitations":["WOLA’s press release summarizes its report and recommendations; it does not provide the full underlying dataset in the supplied text."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0c1a02b661d37eae","start_unit":1,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Expansión summarized controversies involving López Obrador’s relatives, including alleged benefits from contracts, cash deliveries, contractor housing, and credits; it reported that friends of Andrés López Beltrán obtained more than 100 million pesos in contracts and that López Obrador defended his relatives, denied corruption, and said family members should assume responsibility for their own affairs.","question_ids":["4B.2","5B.5","7B.3","7B.4","7B.5","7B.8","7B.9","7B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Published in May 2023 and directly summarizes controversies relevant to the target year, while including earlier episodes for context.","ruler_attribution":"The article reports López Obrador’s public defenses and denials alongside allegations involving his relatives and associates.","limitations":["The source is a journalistic summary of allegations and statements, not a final adjudication of each controversy."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9a14c009a0151b1e","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"López Obrador accused elite journalists of sabotaging his government, alleged that Carlos Loret de Mola’s income came from corruption, asked INAI to investigate and disclose the journalist’s income and assets, and said opposition and free expression were legitimate while describing the journalist and associated media as corrupt political actors.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The statement dates from February 2022 and supplies relevant context for the administration’s treatment of critical media during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The statements were made personally by López Obrador in a presidential conference and letter to INAI.","limitations":["The source records allegations and rhetoric, not proof that the journalist’s income derived from corruption or that an unlawful investigation occurred."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied sources are heterogeneous reports, advocacy statements, and journalistic summaries; facts are attributed to the reporting institution or speaker and are not independently scored.","Several documents concern earlier years or later publication dates but contain material evidence about institutional trajectories and conduct relevant to López Obrador’s 2023 period."]}
